one_liner: Chain of 1,200 sq ft neighbourhood primary-care clinics with in-house diagnostics and a pharmacy; three clinics open in Hyderabad suburbs.
sub_sector: Healthcare services / primary-care clinic chain with diagnostics and pharmacy
ask: INR 3 Cr at INR 18 Cr post-money
business_model: Owned clinics earning consultation, diagnostics and pharmacy revenue (at maturity 62% consultations+diagnostics, 38% pharmacy, per deck). Capex INR 28 L per clinic; first clinic broke even in month 8.

founders.name: Dr. Lakshmi Reddy
founders.background_claimed: MBBS, 8 years in family medicine. Designs the clinical protocols.
founders.background_verified: Not verified. LinkedIn link is a placeholder. A 'Dr K Lakshmi Reddy' (MBBS, MD General Medicine, '5 Yrs Experience') is listed as a consultant at Continental Hospitals, Hyderabad, but nothing links her to CareCorner and the profile does not match the claimed 8 years in family medicine; treated as an unrelated same-name person. No medical council registration number provided to check.

founders.name: Vikram Rao
founders.background_claimed: 6 years in operations at a hospital chain. Runs site selection and rollout.
founders.background_verified: Not verified. LinkedIn link is a placeholder; hospital chain not named; search for name + CareCorner + Hyderabad found nothing.

claims.text: Dr. Lakshmi Reddy (CEO) is an MBBS with 8 years in family medicine.
claims.note: Deck and form agree. No council registration or LinkedIn to verify.

claims.text: Vikram Rao (COO) has 6 years in operations at a hospital chain.
A same-name doctor, Dr K Lakshmi Reddy, is a consultant in internal medicine at Continental Hospitals, Hyderabad; it could not be established that she is the CareCorner founder.
claims.note: Profile lists MD General Medicine and 5 years' experience, and a current hospital affiliation, which does not fit 'full-time since August 2025' and '8 years in family medicine'. Do not treat as verification either way.

claims.text: Both founders' LinkedIn links are placeholders and no public footprint was found for either.
Deck positions CareCorner as clinics 'for Tier-2 India', but the three clinics are in Hyderabad suburbs.
claims.note: Hyderabad is a metro; the SAM is built on Tier-2 cities of Telangana, AP and Karnataka where no clinic is yet open. The deck's '20 to 40 km' travel problem is unlikely to describe Hyderabad suburbs.

claims.text: Three clinics generated INR 9.8 L revenue in October 2026; the first clinic reached monthly breakeven in month 8.
claims.note: Deck and form agree. Implies ~INR 3.3 L per clinic per month.

claims.text: The month-by-month revenue trend (Jun 3.9 L to Oct 9.8 L) is an assumed ordering; the PDF extraction listed values as 9.8, 8.6, 7.0, 3.9, 5.2.
claims.note: Only October (9.8 L) is confirmed by the form. Growth shape, and whether there was a dip, must be confirmed from clinic P&Ls.

claims.text: Mature clinic revenue is projected at INR 1.4 Cr a year, 62% consultations and diagnostics, 38% pharmacy.
claims.note: Our arithmetic: current ~INR 3.3 L/clinic/month annualises to ~INR 39 L, so maturity assumes ~3.6x today's average clinic. SOM of INR 35 Cr (25 clinics x INR 1.4 Cr) rests on this.

claims.text: Twelve-month target is 8 clinics, INR 45 L monthly revenue and 3 clinics at breakeven.
claims.note: Implies ~INR 5.6 L per clinic per month on average with 5 new clinics still ramping; 70% above today's per-clinic average.

claims.text: Patient acquisition cost is about INR 210 per new patient; 45% local doctor referrals, 35% WhatsApp and Google listings, 20% health camps.
claims.note: Deck slide 7 gives the same figures. Patient retention/visit frequency (the deciding metric for primary care) is not given.

claims.text: Capex is INR 28 L per clinic, funded by angels and an INR 40 L bank loan; existing funding is angels INR 60 L plus bank loan INR 40 L.
claims.note: Consistent: 3 clinics x 28 L = 84 L against INR 1 Cr raised/borrowed. 47% of the INR 3 Cr ask (INR 1.41 Cr) for five clinics matches INR 28 L each.

claims.text: Angels hold 25% for INR 60 L (implied ~INR 2.4 Cr post-money); the founders now seek INR 18 Cr post-money.
claims.note: Our arithmetic: ~7.5x step-up in valuation within about a year.

claims.text: Team of 14 including 3 doctors.
claims.note: Deck and form agree. With three clinics, each relies on one doctor; doctor retention is a founder-named key risk.

claims.text: Both founders full-time since August 2025, when the company was incorporated; no prior startup experience.
Each clinic includes in-house diagnostics with same-day results and a pharmacy.
claims.note: Diagnostics and pharmacy each carry their own licensing (lab registration, drug licence); none is mentioned.

claims.text: Market sizing: TAM INR 1.14 lakh Cr, SAM INR 5,400 Cr, with household spend estimated from clinic billing and a 90-household survey.
claims.note: Arithmetic checks (190M x INR 6,000; 9M x INR 6,000). The INR 6,000/household input rests on a 90-household survey.

claims.text: Telangana has adopted the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act; all healthcare facilities must register with the District Registering Authority, including diagnostic laboratories.
claims.note: Article dated June 2022. CareCorner does not mention registration status for its clinics or labs.

claims.text: Hyderabad health authorities found ~224 private hospitals operating without mandatory registration in January 2026, issuing show-cause notices and ordering temporary shutdowns.
claims.note: Shows registration is actively enforced in CareCorner's city.

claims.text: Preventify, a Kerala clinic chain for Tier-2/3 India with three clinics, raised INR 2 Cr pre-seed (Feb 2026) led by PedalStart.
claims.note: Closest comparable: same clinic count and stage, raised at a smaller ask.

claims.text: Hoola Health (paediatric primary care with diagnostics) raised USD 5 M led by Peak XV's Surge and plans 30 more clinics including in Hyderabad.
claims.note: A funded clinic chain entering CareCorner's city.

claims.text: Founder-listed key risks: capital intensity, doctor retention and slower ramp in new locations.
Founders offer clinic-level P&Ls and are in conversation with two healthcare-focused funds.
Sector selected as 'Other (Healthcare)', consistent with an owned clinic chain (classified here as other).

gaps.why_it_matters: Clinical leadership is core to the model; the CEO's medical registration and the COO's hospital-chain operations record are unverified.
gaps.ask_founder: Please share Dr Reddy's Telangana/NMC medical registration number and real LinkedIn profiles; which hospital chain did Vikram work at, in what role?

gaps.what: Regulatory registrations for clinics, labs and pharmacies
gaps.why_it_matters: Telangana enforces Clinical Establishments Act registration (including diagnostic labs) with shutdowns and fines; pharmacy is 38% of mature revenue and needs a drug licence.
searched: web: Telangana clinical establishments registration act private clinics diagnostics
gaps.ask_founder: Are all three clinics and their labs registered under the Clinical Establishments Act, and do the pharmacies hold retail drug licences? Is any lab NABL-accredited?

gaps.what: Clinic-level P&Ls and actual monthly revenue series
gaps.why_it_matters: The chart's month order is an extraction assumption; ramp per clinic is the deciding metric for a clinic chain.
gaps.ask_founder: Send the clinic-level P&Ls you offered: revenue, gross margin and EBITDA by clinic by month since opening, with opening dates.

gaps.why_it_matters: The family-doctor thesis depends on repeat visits; CAC of INR 210 means little without visits per patient per year.
gaps.ask_founder: What share of patients return within 90 days, and how many visits per registered family per year?

gaps.what: Basis for INR 1.4 Cr mature clinic revenue
gaps.why_it_matters: Current clinics average ~INR 39 L annualised; the SOM, breakeven and 12-month plan all depend on a 3.6x ramp.
gaps.ask_founder: What does your best clinic make today, and what patient volume per day does INR 1.4 Cr require?

gaps.why_it_matters: The pitch is Tier-2 India but every clinic is in Hyderabad suburbs; ramp in a genuine Tier-2 town is untested.
gaps.ask_founder: Where will the five new clinics open, and why will a Tier-2 town ramp like a Hyderabad suburb?

gaps.what: Bank loan terms and personal guarantees
gaps.why_it_matters: An INR 40 L loan on a pre-seed balance sheet may carry founder guarantees or covenants that shape use of the new round.
gaps.ask_founder: What are the INR 40 L loan's rate, tenor, collateral and guarantees?

gaps.why_it_matters: No website (placeholder), Google listing or MCA record for CareCorner Health Pvt. Ltd. was found, though the deck claims 35% of patients come from WhatsApp and Google listings.
gaps.ask_founder: Share the CIN and the Google Business listings for the three clinics.

research_notes: Founder/company searches returned no CareCorner footprint (placeholder links). One same-name doctor found at Continental Hospitals; not linkable and recorded as unverifiable. Deck and form agree on every number; the main inconsistency is Tier-2 positioning vs Hyderabad-suburb clinics, plus the assumed chart ordering. Web quotes were extracted via a fetch tool and should be re-verified with verify_web.
